## Summary

Ensure the herdr audit-freshness predicate enforces the canonical "at-or-near"
semantics and is the **single source of truth** shared by both the icon display
and the downtime (audit-dispatch) worker.

Audit freshness currently lives only in `isAuditFresh()` in
`packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`. It is the basis for the icon display
(`auditIcon` in `icons.ts`) AND is the documented freshness gate reused by the
downtime dispatch audit tier (`selectAuditCandidate` /
`getNextAuditCandidate` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, which
treats `!isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` as "needs a fresh `/skill:audit`").

Running an audit itself bumps the work item's `updatedAt` to within a fraction
of a second of its `auditedAt` (`wl audit-set` + `wl update --audit-text` +
the verdict-driven status transition). A freshness rule that requires a strict
gap on one side (e.g. only `auditedAt` comfortably ahead of `updatedAt`) can
therefore disagree with the just-persisted state. The canonical fix in
SorraAgents (SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4) treats an audit as fresh when its
`auditedAt` is **at or near** the item's `updatedAt` (within a small
tolerance) because a near-simultaneous `updatedAt` bump is the audit's own
persistence write.

This item makes ContextHub's herdr audit-freshness logic follow the same
at-or-near rule so the icon display and the downtime dispatcher agree, and
never disagree on a just-persisted audit.

## Expected behaviour

- `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` returns true (fresh) when `auditedAt`
  is at-or-near `updatedAt` within a small, named tolerance (the audit's own
  persistence write), and false otherwise.
- The icon (`auditIcon` in `icons.ts`) shows the fresh icon for a
  just-persisted audit (no longer shows the stale glyph for an audit the run
  just persisted).
- The downtime audit candidate selection (`selectAuditCandidate` /
  `getNextAuditCandidate` in `downtime-worker.ts`) uses the SAME
  `isAuditFresh` predicate, so a just-persisted fresh audit is NOT a dispatch
  candidate (no redundant `/skill:audit` re-run).
- Only one freshness definition exists; neither consumer re-implements its
  own comparison.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `isAuditFresh` in `icons.ts` treats `auditedAt` at-or-near `updatedAt`
   (within a documented tolerance constant) as fresh, covering the
   audit-persistence case (`auditedAt ~ updatedAt`, delta well under the
   tolerance).
2. A unit test asserts `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` is true for a
   just-persisted audit (auditedAt and updatedAt differ by milliseconds).
3. A unit test asserts a genuinely stale audit (item updated well after the
   audit) is still false (stale), unchanged.
4. `selectAuditCandidate` / `getNextAuditCandidate` in `downtime-worker.ts`
   continue to use the imported `isAuditFresh` as the sole filter; a
   just-persisted fresh item is excluded from candidates.
5. Both consumers import the same helper; no competing freshness comparison
   is introduced in the dispatch or icon paths.

## Notes / Open questions

- `isAuditFresh` currently hard-codes a magic `60000` ms literal. Prefer
  naming a constant (e.g. `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS`) and routing
  both consumers through it.
- Reconcile the comparison shape of `isAuditFresh` (`auditTime > updateTime -
  buffer`) with the canonical at-or-near semantics from the SorraAgents fix so
  both projects express the same intent. Confirm the target semantics with the
  operator before implementing.

## References

- discovered-from: SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4 (SorraAgents audit_runner child
  freshness at-or-near fix) — canonical reference implementation.
- related-to: WL-0MSI9FK2Q0074C31 (Audit candidate selection),
  WL-0MSI9WPNI0044R (Audit dispatch tier), parent WL-0MSI8H3HP700K0RG.
data.title: Unify audit-freshness at-or-near logic across icon display and downtime dispatcher

# Intake Brief: Herdr pane title should reflect how it was spawned

## Problem statement

When a pi agent pane is spawned from the Herdr worklist, its title is generic
("Pi Agent" for agent commands, "Command Output" for `!!`/`!` shell commands),
so the user cannot tell at a glance how each pane was spawned or which work
item it belongs to. The downtime dispatcher already names its panes
(`Downtime plan` / `Downtime intake` / `Downtime audit`), but the manual spawn
paths do not.

## Users

- **Herdr users running skill/workflow commands** — want pane titles that
  identify the spawn source (manual vs downtime), the skill invoked, and the
  target work item, so multi-pane sessions are navigable.
  - As a user, I trigger `/skill:implement <id>` from the worklist, and the
    new pane is titled `Manually triggered implement <title> - WL-<id>` so I
    can find it among other panes.
  - As a user running a `!!` shell shortcut (e.g. audit approve/reject), the
    resulting pane identifies the command and work item instead of a generic
    "Command Output".
  - As a user, I see downtime-dispatched panes in the same descriptive format
    so all pi panes follow one naming convention.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Agent-command panes spawned from the worklist (skill shortcuts,
   `/intake`, `/plan`) get a descriptive title of the form
   `Manually triggered <skill> <work item title> - <id>`; the skill token is
   derived from the command (e.g. `/skill:implement` → `implement`).
2. Free-form `/prompt:` commands produce a title like
   `Manually triggered prompt <first words…>` (truncated), or a sensible
   fallback when no prompt text remains.
3. `!!`/`!` shell-command panes (routed via `run-in-pane.sh`) get a
   descriptive title instead of the generic "Command Output", identifying the
   command/work item where available.
4. Downtime-dispatched panes are updated from the short `Downtime <kind>` to
   the same full format (e.g. `Downtime triggered <skill> <title> - <id>`),
   keeping one consistent convention across all pi panes.
5. Title length is bounded (truncated) so pane names stay usable in the Herdr
   UI; commands without a work item still get a descriptive-but-safe title.
6. Unit tests cover title construction for each spawn path (manual skill,
   `/prompt:`, `!!`/`!` shell, downtime), including missing work-item and
   missing-title cases.
7. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No change to the interactive `open-pi-agent.sh` pane (keeps "Pi Agent").
- The work-item title must be sourced without adding blocking process spawns
  in the TUI loop — prefer threading the already-loaded item title from the
  worklist state into the spawn path.
- Pane titles must remain safe for herdr pane-rename (no shell metacharacter
  injection; the rename already runs with quoting).

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` supports `--pane-name` (default
  `Pi Agent`) and renames the pane after spawning pi.
- Manual agent dispatches go through `buildSendToPiArgs` in
  `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`, which does **not** pass `--pane-name` →
  panes are named `Pi Agent`.
- The downtime worker (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) uses
  `buildDowntimePaneArgs` → `--pane-name "Downtime <kind>"`.
- `!!`/`!` shell commands route through `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh`
  which renames the pane `Command Output` (override via `RUN_IN_PANE_NAME`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `resolveAndRouteCommand` has the selected
  item (with `id` + `title`) at dispatch time, but `onCommand` only forwards
  `(command, model)`.

## Desired change

- Extend the agent-command spawn path (`buildSendToPiArgs` call site in
  `index.ts`) to pass `--pane-name` with a title built from a descriptor
  (`Manually triggered`), the skill name parsed from the command, the work
  item title, and the work-item ID.
- Thread the selected item's title from `worklist.ts` into the dispatch
  (extend the `onCommand` seam or pass a prebuilt title) so no extra `wl`
  spawn is needed.
- Add the same `--pane-name` behavior to the `!!`/`!` shell path
  (`run-in-pane.sh` invocation in `index.ts`), replacing "Command Output".
- Update `buildDowntimePaneArgs` / the downtime spawn to the full format so
  downtime panes match (e.g. `Downtime triggered <kind> <title> - <id>`).
- Centralize title construction (descriptor + skill + title + id, with
  truncation) so all spawn paths share one function.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — agent/pane dispatch; add `--pane-name` to
  `buildSendToPiArgs` and the `run-in-pane.sh` spawn.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `resolveAndRouteCommand` / `onCommand`
  seam; forward the selected item's title (or a prebuilt pane title).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `buildDowntimePaneArgs` / pane
  name; adopt the full format (`Downtime triggered …`).
- `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh` — pane-name plumbing if the title
  is passed via env/arg.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`
  — tests for the new title construction per spawn path.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9` — "Herdr worklist: track agents spawned per work item
  and show their status icon". Related: pane spawn plumbing (pane-id capture)
  in the same dispatch path.
- `WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG` — "Allow /skill:audit on complete/in_review items
  without a valid audit". Related: downtime audit tier uses the same
  `buildDowntimePaneArgs` path that will adopt the full title format.
- `WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K` — downtime worker (dispatch panes open in the
  resolved worklog root); pane naming originates here.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the work-item title is threaded from the worklist state
  (already loaded) rather than fetched via `wl show` — avoids extra spawns in
  the TUI loop. If threading proves invasive, fall back to `wl show` at spawn
  (documented tradeoff: extra subprocess per dispatch).
- **Risk:** long work-item titles make pane names unusable — mitigated by
  truncation (bounded length) in the shared title builder.
- **Assumption:** `/prompt:` panes use `Manually triggered prompt <first
  words…>` per user confirmation.
- **Assumption:** `!!`/`!` panes keep the manual descriptor with the command
  and work-item context; exact token order to be confirmed during planning.
- **Scope-creep guard:** interactive `open-pi-agent.sh` naming is explicitly
  out of scope; any further spawn-source descriptors discovered during
  implementation should be recorded as linked work items, not folded in.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which panes should get descriptive titles? (a) Only agent-command
  panes spawned from skill shortcuts (`/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`,
  `/prompt:`), (b) also the `!!`/`!` shell-command panes (currently
  'Command Output'), (c) also the interactive `open-pi-agent.sh` pane
  (currently 'Pi Agent')?"
  - Answer (user, interactive reply): **b** — agent-command panes AND the
    `!!`/`!` shell-command panes; the interactive open-pi-agent pane is
    excluded.
- Q2: "Should the downtime dispatcher's panes be updated to match the new
  full format (e.g. `Downtime triggered plan <title> - WL-<id>`), or keep its
  current short form (`Downtime plan`) while only the manual path gets the
  descriptive format?"
  - Answer (user, interactive reply): **update** — downtime panes adopt the
    same full format for a single consistent convention.
- Q3: "Free-form `/prompt:` commands have no skill name and may have no
  work-item ID. What should their title be (e.g. `Manually triggered prompt
  <first words…>`), or should they keep the default 'Pi Agent'?"
  - Answer (user, interactive reply): **use the suggested title**
    (`Manually triggered prompt <first words…>`).

---

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I** – Detail view ToC for Related Docs (completed)
- **WL-0MMLXTBCH0F4NV3T** – Migrate GitHub helpers to use throttler (completed)
- **WL-0MMS4EVN10RG8T47** – Migration & Safety Flow (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-Herdr-pane-title-should-reflect-how-it-was-spawned-WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y.md` — matched: already, descriptors, dispatcher, downtime, end (+18 more)
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MSI4TAT70058921-rename-podcast-editing-tab-to-worklog/packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: already, downtime, end, herdr, how (+14 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: already, downtime, end, herdr, how (+14 more)

## Summary

**Re-scoped** follow-up to the completed twin **WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO** (shipped in
v1.0.13, commit `9e8ca646`, epic WL-0MTFNII4X00632CG), which already delivered this
item's original AC1–AC3 (the unbounded same-timestamp conflict loop and the
unattributed-soft-delete override). Those are now shipped; this item is narrowed to the
**residual** that the earlier fix left in place.

**Residual defect:** `mergeSameTimestampItems` still writes a **fresh wall-clock
`updatedAt`** whenever a non-`sortIndex` field is reconciled and the merged result
differs from local (`src/sync.ts` ~L833):

```ts
if (nonSortIndexMerged && !mergedEqualsLocal) {
  merged.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString();   // <-- wall-clock stamp on a merge
}
```

A merge is not a user edit. Stamping "now" silently re-timestamps audit-fresh items and
marks valid audits stale, and it feeds further timestamp churn on subsequent syncs.

## Problem

Observed on 2026-09-21: a single sync (`18:35:58 → 18:36:17`) logged **244 conflicts**
and re-timestamped **95 items** to `2026-09-21T18:36:06` (48 of them `completed`).
**14 `completed`/`in_review` items lost audit freshness purely from merge churn** — e.g.
*Sync: regression guard…* (`WL-0MSOYWZTH003JFVD`) was audited 2026-08-31, had no activity
since, yet became "stale" because the merge moved `updatedAt`.

Because `updatedAt` underpins `isAuditFresh` (until the content-fingerprint gate lands,
P1), merge churn drives false staleness → redundant downtime re-audits → more writes →
more churn.

## Expected behaviour

- A merge must **never** introduce a wall-clock `updatedAt`. A same-timestamp merge
  inherits an existing timestamp (the two sides are equal by definition), so repeated
  syncs of the same divergence are **quiescent**.
- Merged content still converges on both sides.
- Audit freshness is unaffected by a merge that did not change user-authored content.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `mergeSameTimestampItems` no longer calls `new Date().toISOString()` for
  `updatedAt`; the merged item inherits the (equal) existing timestamp.
- AC2: Regression test: two divergent copies with the same `updatedAt` (differing in one
  non-`sortIndex` field) merged repeatedly are quiescent — `updatedAt` never advances and
  content converges.
- AC3: Regression test: a same-timestamp conflict resolved to remote content leaves
  `updatedAt` unchanged and `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` true for a prior valid
  audit.
- AC4: `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` continues to inherit the winning side's timestamp
  (no wall-clock); an explicit assertion is added.
- AC5: Full existing test suite passes, including the sync convergence + delete-protection
  tests shipped under WL-0MTFNII4X00632CG.

## Notes / open questions

- The original bump existed so the merged side would be unambiguously "newer" on the next
  sync. With both sides writing the merged result, convergence should hold without it;
  confirm via the AC2 quiescence test.
- A same-timestamp `sortIndex`-only conflict already never bumps (unchanged).

## References

- discovered-from: WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE
- shipped predecessor (do not re-implement): WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO (completed/done,
  v1.0.13, `9e8ca646`), WL-0MTFNII4X00632CG, WL-0MT2KZH0I005XUWE
- related-to: WL-0MUBVH5S0008NQ9K (P1 — content-fingerprint freshness gate)
- evidence: `.worklog/logs/sync.log` (2026-09-21T18:35:58 → 18:36:17)
data.title: Sync merges must not re-timestamp audit-fresh items (remove wall-clock updatedAt bump)

## Summary

`npm run build` in `packages/herdr` exits 2 with 84 `TS6059` errors (`File ... is not under 'rootDir' '/home/.../packages/herdr/src'`).

## Root cause

`packages/herdr/tsconfig.json` sets `rootDir: ./src` and includes `src/**/*.ts`, which includes the `.test.ts` files. Several herdr test files (e.g. `src/implement-tier-blocked-exclusion.test.ts`, worklist tests) import shared CLI test helpers from the repo root (`../../tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts`, `../../src/*`). Those files are pulled into the compilation graph but lie outside `rootDir`, producing TS6059 for every import. tsc still emits the in-root files to `dist/`, but the `cp src/shortcuts.json dist/shortcuts.json` step of the build script never runs (tsc exits non-zero), leaving `dist/shortcuts.json` stale.

## Expected behaviour

- `cd packages/herdr && npm run build` exits 0 and copies `src/shortcuts.json` → `dist/shortcuts.json`.

## Implementation notes

- Exclude test files from the herdr build: add `"exclude": ["**/*.test.ts"]` to `packages/herdr/tsconfig.json` (the test files are compiled/run by vitest, not needed in dist). Verify `npm run build` exits 0 and `dist/` contains no `.test.js` files.
- Check whether `packages/shared/tsconfig.json` has the same pattern (it builds cleanly today — likely no test files there).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cd packages/herdr && npm run build` exits 0.
- [ ] `dist/shortcuts.json` is copied on every build.
- [ ] `npx vitest run packages/herdr` still passes (tests unaffected by the exclude).

Discovered from: WL-0MSNULGSM00018I4

# Intake Brief: Sync — Regression Guard

## Problem Statement

When `wl sync` merges remote state that is newer than local, it can silently import regressions: fields the local store had set to non-default values (e.g. `effort: 'Small'`, `status: completed`) get overwritten with defaults by a stale/divergent second store, as observed Aug 6–10, 2026 on the llm worklog ref.

## Users

- **Primary**: Operators of multi-store worklog setups — anyone running more than one `wl sync` instance against the same remote.
- **Secondary**: Producers/reviewers whose audit results (status/stage transitions) are silently reverted by stale syncs.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. During merge, for each incoming remote item with a newer `updatedAt` than local, detect regressions where a field moves from a non-default value to its default on the fields that participate in the merge: `status`/`stage` (non-default → default, e.g. `completed/in_review` → `open/idea`), `priority` (non-default → default), and `assignee` (set → unset).

   **`effort`/`risk` (producer resolution, 2026-08-23): stay PERMANENTLY EXCLUDED from the merge field lists** — ping-pong prevention by construction. A remote `effort: ''` / `risk: ''` never enters the merge; local non-default values are always kept. The guard additionally REPORTS any attempted effort/risk regression (remote non-empty → default) as a protected conflict (local kept, nothing imported) for observability, but no override path is needed for these two fields since they cannot be imported through the merge.
2. On detecting a regression, `wl sync` refuses to import that item's regressed fields: reports the conflict (item id, field, old local value, new remote default value) and keeps the local value. An explicit override flag (`--accept-regressions` or equivalent) allows the operator to accept the regression.
3. Genuine concurrent edits (both stores changed different non-default fields, or both changed the same field to different non-default values) still merge and re-timestamp exactly as today — this guard must NOT change legitimate conflict resolution.
4. The regression guard applies only to the `import()`/merge path used by `wl sync` — it does NOT affect explicit user `wl update` commands, which remain authoritative.
5. Unit tests cover: (a) newer remote with `effort: ''` against local `effort: 'Small'` → local kept (exclusion by construction), conflict REPORTED as protected, remote value NOT imported; (b) newer remote with `status: open` against local `completed` → refused, local kept, conflict reported; (c) both sides non-default differing → normal merge + re-timestamp (no regression path — guard must NOT alter legitimate conflict resolution); (d) override flag accepts the regression for merge-participating fields only; (e) `--dry-run` reports the same refusals.
6. Manual verification: sync against the known commit `5fc880a` (effort/risk cleared) → regressions refused and reported; sync against `54b1375` (restored values) → no regression flags.

## Constraints

- Must not change behavior for legitimate concurrent edits — the guard is regression-only, not conflict-resolution.
- Must be deterministic: dry-run and normal sync report the same refusals.
- Does NOT prevent a second store from pushing — it prevents the primary store from absorbing regressive state.
- Complements the identity gate (WL-0MSOYWWS4009HTCB) — the identity gate catches the writer; this guard catches the damage even if the writer's identity is unknown.

## Existing State

The merge functions (`mergeSameTimestampItems`, `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` in `src/sync.ts`) already implement a non-default-preference heuristic: when one side has a non-default value and the other has a default, the non-default is preserved. The `isDefaultValue` helper in `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` classifies empty strings, `undefined`, and empty arrays as defaults.

The merge field arrays include `status`, `stage`, `priority`, and `assignee` — these fields **already** keep the local non-default value when the remote sends a default (via the `!localIsDefault && remoteIsDefault` branch). They do **not** produce an explicit regression report — the local value is silently kept.

The merge field arrays do **not** include `effort` or `risk` — these fields are never merged at all; the local value is always preserved regardless of the remote.

**Contradiction — RESOLVED (producer decision, 2026-08-23)**: The 13-field merge list currently excludes `effort`/`risk` (code-confirmed), yet the original ACs listed them as regression targets. Producer directive: *"The goal is to prevent ping-pong — do what you need to."* Resolution: **Reading A** — `effort`/`risk` remain excluded from the merge lists; adding them to the merge would re-introduce the ping-pong (the DB re-timestamp amplifier in `hasWorkItemChanged` already tracks these fields, so a single unguarded import becomes the newest record and propagates). The guard therefore targets the merge-participating fields (`status`/`stage`/`priority`/`assignee`), and `effort`/`risk` regressions are reported as protected (local kept). Effort/risk merge-participation is a non-goal.

## Desired Change

Add a regression detection layer on top of the merge path that:
- Identifies fields regressing from non-default → default in newer remote state, for the merge-participating fields: `status`/`stage`/`priority`/`assignee`
- Reports conflicts with details (item id, field, old value, new value)
- Refuses to import regressed fields (keeping local) unless overridden (`--accept-regressions`, merge-participating fields only)
- Preserves all existing merge behavior for non-regression cases
- Reports (without importing) attempted `effort`/`risk` regressions as protected — these fields remain excluded from the merge lists (non-goal: adding them back)

## Risks & Assumptions

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| Regression detection logic breaks existing merge behavior | High | Unit tests must verify non-regression cases still merge correctly (AC3) |
| Scope creep: "regression" definition might be too broad (e.g., should a valid transition like `in_progress → open` count as regression?) | Medium | Strict definition: only non-default → default transitions count |
| Override flag (`--accept-regressions`) could be misused, allowing silent data loss | Medium | Require explicit flag; report what was accepted in output |
| **DECIDED**: effort/risk must NOT be added to the merge list | — | Producer resolution 2026-08-23: adding them re-introduces ping-pong (DB re-timestamp amplifier `hasWorkItemChanged` tracks these fields; one unguarded import becomes the newest record) |
| `isDefaultValue` may not correctly identify defaults for all fields (e.g., custom stages) | Low | Only built-in defaults (`open`, `idea`, `medium`, empty strings) are guarded; custom stages fall through to normal merge |
| **Scope-creep risk**: The guard could be extended to "merge strategies" or general conflict-policy work — those are separate concerns. | Medium | Record as future work items; do not implement here |

**Assumptions**:
- The `isDefaultValue` function correctly classifies all default values for the fields in question
- Regression detection can be cleanly layered on top of existing merge logic without restructuring
- The operator will accept a new CLI flag for override

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/sync.ts` — `mergeSameTimestampItems`, `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`: add regression detection alongside the existing merge logic (field lists UNCHANGED for `effort`/`risk` — exclusion is the ping-pong prevention)
- `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` — `isDefaultValue`: may need no changes (already classifies empties as defaults)
- `src/commands/sync.ts` — CLI flag for `--accept-regressions`, conflict reporting in output
- `tests/sync-regression-guard.test.ts` — new test file for regression detection scenarios

## Related Work

As an operator, I do not want a transient failure in the downtime dispatch pipeline to strand a work item in `in_progress` with no agent working it and no automatic recovery.

## Background

- dispatchClaimedTier (packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts) pipeline: CAS claim → marker write → spawn.
- Gap 1 from the dispatch decision-point evaluation: if the marker write fails (D16) AFTER the CAS claim succeeds, the outcome is reason 'marker-write-failed' and the item stays `in_progress` — but the claim is never rolled back. The item is then invisible to every later tier: plan/implement tiers select `status === 'open'`, the audit tier selects `completed`. Only manual intervention recovers it.
- Same class of issue on 'spawn-failed' (D17): the marker stands (kind `implement`/`plan`/`audit` at the dispatched-at stage), so even after a human reverts the item to `open`, the dispatched-marker exclusion keeps it out of selection until the stage changes — a transient send-to-pi.sh failure (e.g. ENOENT) permanently removes a never-worked item from the idle-slot queue.
- Existing design intent (RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT design point 2): "an unmarked item is never dispatched" — this is sound; the gap is the missing RECOVERY path, not the fail-closed abort.

## Design notes

- Option A (rollback): on 'marker-write-failed', restore the item to its pre-claim state (CAS reverse: `wl update <id> --status open --if-status in_progress [--if-stage ...]`) so the next idle period can select it again.
- Option B (requeue for spawn-failed): on 'spawn-failed', write a distinct marker variant (e.g. `outcome: 'spawn-failed'` entries are already appended) and have the marker-exclusion readers treat a spawn-failed marker as NON-excluding (item is re-eligible) while still logging the failure — the rolling log already distinguishes attempted vs opened (WL-0MSLWJ3I70031Z8U AC2).
- Both options preserve the fail-closed invariant (a marker-less item is never dispatched twice concurrently); the CAS claim already serializes re-selection.
- Decide and document whether the re-dispatch window should be immediate (next idle) or after a short backoff to avoid spawn-failure hot loops.

## Acceptance criteria

1. 'marker-write-failed' leaves the item in a state selectable by a future tier (rolled back to open+original stage, or equivalently recovered) — never stranded in_progress with no agent.
2. 'spawn-failed' does not permanently exclude the item from selection; the failure trace remains in the rolling log and the outcome is still not success.
3. No regression: an item with a STANDING success marker is still excluded (never double-dispatched); CAS claim still serializes concurrent panes.
4. Tests cover marker-write-failed and spawn-failed recovery paths end-to-end (claim → failure → re-selection on the next idle period).

The downtime dispatcher consistently selects and dispatches work items that do not appear in the herdr extensions selection list, so two first-class "next most important item" selectors disagree. # Scheduled prompts: add time-of-day dispatch (time window) to scheduled-prompts tier

## Problem statement

The scheduled-prompts tier (WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX; `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, `templates/scheduled-prompts.json`) only supports best-effort frequency in whole days (`intervalDays` via `isDueScheduledPrompt`: due iff `now - lastTriggeredAt >= intervalDays`). There is no way to pin a prompt to a time of day, so a daily standup cannot be made to run at a specific wall-clock time (e.g. 06:05) and instead fires whenever the next idle slot appears after the interval elapses — too early/late for a daily standup window.

## Users

- Operators who want a prompt (notably the daily standup, `/skill:standup`) to run at a specific time of day, not just once per N days whenever an idle slot appears.

### User stories

- As an operator, I want to add an optional `time` field (e.g. `06:05`) to a scheduled-prompt entry so the system dispatches it in the first available idle window **after** that time, so the standup runs at 06:05 each day.
- As an operator, when `time` is absent the existing behaviour is unchanged (due iff `now - last >= intervalDays`), so existing entries like `/skill:refactor` keep working without config changes.
- As an operator, I want `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` and provisioned `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` to set `/skill:standup` to 06:05, so a fresh worklog gets the correct daily standup time.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add optional `time?: string` to `ScheduledPrompt` (`packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts`). When absent, behaviour is identical to today (backward-compatible). Valid values are wall-clock `HH:MM` 24-hour times (e.g. `06:05`); entries with an invalid `time` are skipped with a logged warning (fail-closed, never a crash), consistent with invalid `intervalDays`/prompt handling (AC7 of WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX).
2. Extend due-check semantics (`isDueScheduledPrompt` / `getDueScheduledPrompt`): an entry with `time` is due only when BOTH (a) `now - lastTriggeredAt >= intervalDays * DAY_MS` (same interval gate as today) AND (b) `now` is at or after the `time` on the calendar day of `now` (local wall-clock). If `now` is before `time` today and the interval gate is otherwise satisfied, the entry is NOT due — it becomes due in the first idle window at/after `time`. A dispatched entry is NOT due again until the next calendar day's `time` has been reached and the interval has again elapsed (so a 06:05 daily entry dispatched at 07:00 today is not due again at 08:00 today).
3. `lastTriggeredAt` semantics ensure once-per-interval: after a timed dispatch, the interval comparison uses the actual dispatch time, so a missed `time` (e.g. no idle slot until 08:00) still counts as dispatched for that day and the next due time is tomorrow 06:05 (not 08:00 tomorrow and not immediately). Daily entries with `time` therefore fire at most once per calendar day.
4. Update `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` to include `/skill:standup` with `intervalDays: 1` and `time: "06:05"` (the canonical standup time). `src/commands/init.ts` provisioning remains create-if-absent; `wl init` on an existing repo must not clobber user edits — if the operator has customised scheduled prompts, re-running `wl init` leaves them untouched. New worklogs provisioned after this change get the timed standup entry.
5. Ensure `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` in the current checkout reflects `time: "06:05"` for `/skill:standup` (so the dev branch's live config matches the template).
6. Update documentation/comments to describe the `time` field (README / `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` header / `PLUGIN_GUIDE.md` or equivalent downtime docs) and the "first window after time" semantics, including the backward-compat note when `time` is absent and the local wall-clock interpretation of `HH:MM`.
7. Unit/integration tests cover: parse of `time` (valid, absent, invalid → skipped), due-check with `time` (before-time not due, at/after-time due, interval gate interaction, once-per-day, missed-window becomes tomorrow), backward-compat (no `time` behaves as before), and the timed standup entry in the provisioned template.
8. Full project test suite passes with the new changes (no regressions).

## Constraints

- Follow the worker's existing fail-closed philosophy at every boundary: never dispatch, never throw (mirrors WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX constraints and `scheduled-prompts.ts` header).
- `time` is wall-clock local `HH:MM` (no timezone field, no cron); `lastTriggeredAt` remains UTC ISO-8601 as today. The due check interprets `time` against local calendar day.
- Scheduled tier remains the first dispatch tier, gated by the same fresh-read code-freeze marker; per-process single-flight guard still applies. No new timer infrastructure — reuse `createDowntimeWorker.tick`.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` — `ScheduledPrompt` (id/prompt/intervalDays/lastTriggeredAt), `parseScheduledPrompt`, `isDueScheduledPrompt`, `getDueScheduledPrompt`, `DAY_MS`; no `time` field.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchDowntimeWork` scheduled tier (freeze gate → scheduled → audit → …); `dispatchScheduledPrompt` with atomic `lastTriggeredAt` persist + rolling-log `scheduled` kind.
- `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` + `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` — base set is `/skill:refactor` (intervalDays 3) plus `/skill:standup` (intervalDays 1) with no `time`.
- `src/commands/init.ts` — provisions `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` from the template, create-if-absent (never clobber).

## Desired change

Extend `ScheduledPrompt` with optional `time: "HH:MM"` and update the due-check to be "interval gate AND at-or-after time today" so timed entries dispatch in the first idle window after their wall-clock time. A non-leader's entry is offered at most once per 30min yet is pruned after 5min if no dispatch consumes it — 25min dead window where the leader sees no entry for that project.

Overnight this starved SorraAgents while ContextHub dispatched alone every ~30min (verified Sep 4: SorraAgents offered `SA-0MSQ6K7Z1002H14Z` at 06:39:39 -> dispatched 06:39:41 only when offer was fresh; earlier offers at 23:45,00:08,00:38 etc. were pruned before the next idle dispatch). ## Users

- **Producer / operator** — expects global `critical first, then round-robin across projects` as documented; overnight bias to one project erodes trust and delays other projects' ready work.
- **Herdr user with multiple project tabs open** — wants spare-capacity dispatch shared fairly, not oversubscribing one project's backlog.
- **Maintainer of herdr / downtime-worker / wl** — needs a single consistent contract for cross-project dispatch without TTL/check-in mismatch.

## Goal

Root-cause the recurring `Downtime worker: 3 consecutive wl CLI errors — pausing dispatch for 3600000ms.` events that pause the downtime dispatcher for an hour across multiple projects, and fix the underlying cause so dispatch does not silently stall.

## Problem Statement

Every dispatch attempt in the observed window was followed ~90s later by a 60-minute pause (`three-strike rule`, `DOWNTIME_ERROR_STRIKE_LIMIT=3`). The pauses span every project:

- ContextHub: `14:56:21Z` pause (last dispatch `14:54:45Z`), no further dispatches in the 16:18–18:18Z window (0 in last 2h).
- open_source_llm: 10 dispatches 16:52–17:41Z, each followed ~90s later by a `3 consecutive wl CLI errors — pausing dispatch for 3600000ms.` entry (16:54, 16:58, 17:02, 17:06, 17:10, 17:14, 17:18, 17:22, 17:26, 17:43Z).
- AI_Hell: pause entries at `01:53, 15:23, 16:24, 17:55, 18:57Z` — no successful dispatch since `2026-09-02` (`downtime-round-robin-by-root.json`).
- SorraAgents / Tableau-Card-Engine: last dispatch `09-04 09:41` / `09-03 22:37`, then pause.

The machine-wide coordination file at snapshot held 2 stale ContextHub offers (`955073f2→WL-0MSLPM5ZB003TADT lastUpdated 16:16:45`, `ff2b1535→WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P lastUpdated 18:46:07`) that were never dispatched. The leader lease at the time was stale/expired (a fresh leader `045836e1` acquired only later at `19:03Z`).

The three-strike events log only the generic message — the underlying wl CLI error is NOT captured in `downtime-dispatches.log` (`recordError` writes `{cwd, at, message}` with the generic text). A work item WL-0MTL4PC0Y005GXTI ("Downtime pause log should include underlying wl error details") exists but the cause itself is still unknown: are these `SQLITE_BUSY` lock contentions, WAL growth/checkpoint stalls (WL-0MSG8EG7P002MX2I), sync-conflict loops (WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO — same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt; sync conflict resolution observed in sync.log during the window: `Conflict item=... type=same-timestamp ... chosen=local`), the `wl sync author-identity gate` pre-push block (OSL-0MT5Z8AJ7008LCQQ), or something else?

## User Stories

- As an operator, I want dispatches to stop being silently disabled for an hour, so downtime capacity is actually used.
- As a maintainer, I want the real wl error surfaced in the pause log (not just the generic message), so the cause is diagnosable without deep log archaeology.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Root cause identified** — RCA determines the concrete wl failure mode(s) behind the `3 consecutive wl CLI errors` strikes: reproduce or capture the actual stderr/error of the failing `wl` invocations (poll the logs, check `sync.log`/`downtime-dispatches.log`, run the failing commands manually, inspect `.worklog/logs/sync.log` conflict-resolution output in the window).
2. **Failure surfaces in the pause log** — the pause entry (or an accompanying entry) records the underlying wl error detail (per WL-0MTL4PC0Y005GXTI if not yet closed; otherwise this item supersedes it) so a future pause is diagnosable from the rolling log alone.
3. **Fix applied** — the root cause is fixed (code change in herdr/`wl`/sync/machine-coordination as appropriate): e.g. if `SQLITE_BUSY` → retry/backoff or WAL checkpoint fix; if sync-conflict loop → the same-timestamp merge fix (WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO) is completed; if author-identity gate → OSL-0MT5Z8AJ7008LCQQ fix lands; if leader-lease zombie → the lease-expiry fix (WL-0MTEZ5EK5002RXXD) is confirmed deployed.
4. **Strikes no longer cascade** — after the fix, a normal idle run completes multiple dispatches without a `pausing dispatch for 3600000ms` entry after each one (verified over a 2h window or via unit/integration tests that simulate the failing CLI).
5. **No regressions** — full test suite green (`/skill:test`), including the downtime-worker, coordination-dispatch, and sync-conflict tests.
6. **Durable observability** — the dispatch/error log distinguishes strike causes so a recurrence is visible in one place (ties into the central-log work item).

## Constraints

- Do not disable or loosen the three-strike rule as the fix (it is a safety valve); fix the underlying failure.
- All work in a worktree per the implement workflow; do not edit main checkout.
- Push only to `dev`.

## Existing State / Evidence

- Pause entries (generic message) at the times listed above in each project's `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`.
- `sync.log` shows sync-conflict resolution running DURING the window (same-timestamp conflicts chosen=local, lexicographic tie-break; `itemsUpdated=56`/`49` per sync).
- Related open items: WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO (sync-conflict loop), WL-0MSG8EG7P002MX2I (WAL growth/checkpointing), WL-0MTEZ5EK5002RXXD (leader lease zombie), WL-0MTL4PC0Y005GXTI (pause log lacks wl error detail), OSL-0MT5Z8AJ7008LCQQ (author-identity gate blocks pre-push).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — three-strike rule, `recordError`, `wl` invocations.

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — `appendRollingJsonl` error entries.
- `.worklog/logs/sync.log` + per-project `.worklog/downtime-*.log` — evidence.

## Risks & Assumptions

- Assumption: the strikes share a common cause across projects (same machine, same herdr build, concurrent writers to shared SQLite/coordination files).
- Risk: transient contention that self-heals is hard to repro; mitigation is instrumentation (AC2) + capture real stderr before fixing.

# Implement typing-gated scheduler ticks

Implementation task for WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH — Text inputs miss keypresses when extension is syncing.

## Goal

Introduce a shared `isInputActive()` predicate in `worklist.ts` that returns `true` when any text-input overlay is open, and check it at the top of the `refresh` and `sync` scheduler tick handlers to skip `doSync`/`doRefresh` while the user is typing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — `isInputActive()` predicate:** A new exported (or module-private) function `isInputActive(): boolean` that returns `true` when any text-input overlay is open (`formState !== null || shipItDialog !== null`). The predicate must be defined in the `runWorklistPane` closure scope and accessible by the scheduler tick handlers.
- **AC2 — Scheduler tick gating:** Both the `refresh` and `sync` task `run` callbacks check `isInputActive()` at the top (alongside the existing `paneGate.visible()` check) and return early (skip the tick) when true. No `wl sync` or `doRefresh` is executed while typing.
- **AC3 — md-note-edit coverage:** Since note editing opens a `FormState` (per the codebase), it is already covered by the `formState !== null` check. Document this in code comments.
- **AC4 — No regression when not typing:** When no input overlay is active, existing behaviour is unchanged: auto-refresh (30s default), auto-sync (60s default), visibility/heartbeat/DB-change gates continue as before.
- **AC5 — Downtime/mode-switch audit:** Audit whether `downtimeWorker`/`modeSwitchWorker` ticks need gating. Per analysis: they do NOT trigger list re-render or input loss while a modal is open. Document this decision in a comment next to each task registration.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Add `isInputActive()` predicate and typing gate to scheduler tasks.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — No change expected; add a comment noting gating is caller-side if relevant.

## Implementation Notes

The fix is narrowly scoped: add a guard variable and check in two scheduler task callbacks. The `formState` and `shipItDialog` variables are already in the same closure scope as the scheduler tasks. No changes to `auto-sync.ts` or form handling are needed.

Design decision: skip ticks silently while typing; do NOT queue or trigger an immediate refresh after close. The next regular tick fires normally. This avoids potential infinite refresh loops and matches the existing "skip, don't coalesce" single-flight semantics.

# Summary

The downtime dispatcher treats work items carrying the retired `in_progress` **stage** as dispatchable (`classifyItemForDispatch` → `risk-effort`). The resulting claim is rejected by `wl`'s status/stage validation (`Invalid stage "in_progress"`) and counted as a **hard `wl-error` strike**. Three strikes pause the machine-wide leader for 60 min, and because the item stays at the head of its root's Herdr list it is re-offered at every check-in, so the pause loop is self-perpetuating and idle local-LLM slots go unused.

# Impact / symptom

- Single-slot local LLM idle (`available_slots: 1/1`, slot not processing); the idle gate would pass (`downtimeRequiredFreeSlots: 1`) yet no dispatch occurs.
- Leader healthy (fresh 5-min lease) and coordination offers present, so this is not a liveness/idle-gate failure.
- Repeating `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` entries:
  `{"message":"Downtime worker: 3 consecutive wl CLI errors — pausing dispatch for 3600000ms.","error":"... Invalid stage \"in_progress\" ...","workItemId":"CG-0MT5Y1X5T001M4S6","probeContext":"dispatch-cli"}`
  Observed continuously on 2026-09-12 (e.g. 13:47Z, 15:28–15:29Z, 16:13Z).
- Because the leader iterates offers in file order and the first Tableau offer is the poisoned item, healthy offers from other roots are never reached.

# Root cause

1. Worklog rows still carry the **retired stage `in_progress`** (stage removed by WL-0MTOHS5B4001Y9FX, but existing data was not migrated). 27 such rows exist across 5 roots; 7 have `status=open` (the poison set that strikes).
2. `classifyItemForDispatch` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) maps `stage === 'in_progress'` → `'risk-effort'` (retired-stage recovery path, WL-0MTTSWCJR003OMN7). So the item is deemed dispatchable.
3. Such items are (by grouping/priority) at the head of the root's Herdr list, so the check-in offers them in `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json`.
4. `dispatchClaimedTier` claims via `claimWorkItem` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:769`):
   `wl update <id> --status in_progress --assignee <agent> [--if-stage <expected>]`.
5. `wl`'s update validator (`src/commands/update.ts:310-330`) validates
   `{ status: statusCandidate ?? current.status, stage: stageCandidate ?? current.stage }`.
   With no `--stage`, it falls back to the item's **current** stage `in_progress` →
   `Invalid stage "in_progress". Valid stages: idea, intake_complete, plan_complete, in_review, done.`
   thrown by `src/commands/status-stage-validation.ts`.
6. The claim returns `{ok:false, reason:'error'}` → dispatch outcome `{dispatched:false, reason:'wl-error'}` → one strike (`recordError`). Three consecutive → `pauseAfterPersistentErrors` → 60-min cooldown.
7. The entry is not dropped as "non-dispatchable" (a claim failure is an error, not a classification null), the owning instance re-offers the same head item at its next check-in, so the loop restarts as soon as the pause lifts.

**Secondary defect:** `TIER_EXPECTED['risk-effort'] = { status:'open', stage:'plan_complete' }` is wrong for an item whose actual stage is `in_progress`; even if the update validator accepted the row, the CAS guard would be stale, so the recovery path can never succeed.

# Immediate remediation (applied 2026-09-12)

Normalized the 7 `status=open` + `stage=in_progress` items to the codebase's designated migration target `plan_complete` (compatible with `open` per the built-in `statusStageCompatibility` in `src/config.ts`):

- Tableau-Card-Engine: CG-0MPFM2MK800773X7, CG-0MSTOATDQ005XDET, CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P, CG-0MT5Y1X5T001M4S6, CG-0MTFWBNL30043ZBM, CG-0MTNMBX5Z002U0MH
- ContextHub: WL-0MTMN7W63001FCQR

Remaining `in_progress`-stage rows (20) have `deleted`/`in-progress` status, so `classifyItemForDispatch` returns null and they do not strike — but they still need cleanup for hygiene. Note there is currently **no supported tool** to fix them: `wl doctor --fix` classifies `invalid-stage` (non-empty stage) as `requiresManualFix`, and `wl doctor stage-sync` has no `in_progress` rule.

# Proposed permanent fix

1. **Never strike on an unclassifiable open item.** A stage the dispatcher cannot map to a valid kind must yield a neutral `non-dispatchable`/skip outcome (drop the offer, no `recordError`, no cooldown) and the leader must continue to the next offer.
2. **Fix the retired-stage recovery path.** Either normalize `in_progress` at read time (treat it as `plan_complete` in `DowntimeItemInfo`/`classifyItemForDispatch`) so the claim/validation/CAS all agree, or have the recovery dispatch a migration update (`--stage plan_complete`) rather than a CAS claim on the invalid stage.
3. **Containment:** ensure one poisoned/misclassified offer in one root cannot block dispatch for other roots.
4. **Tooling:** make the retired stage repairable via `wl doctor`/migration and document it.

# Acceptance criteria

1. An open item with an invalid/unknown stage cannot produce a `wl-error` strike or a no-candidate cooldown; it is either classified to a valid kind or dropped neutrally, and the leader proceeds to the next offer.
2. The retired-`in_progress` recovery path claims successfully (or is removed) with no `wl update` validation failure; regression test with a fixture item at stage `in_progress`.
3. Unit test: classif→claim on an `in_progress`-stage item asserts no `wl-error` strike and either a successful dispatch or a neutral skip.
4. A single poisoned offer does not block dispatch for other roots (ordering/containment test).
5. Retired-stage rows are repairable by a supported command/migration; remediation documented.
6. `npm run build` clean and the full suite green.

# References

- WL-0MTOHS5B4001Y9FX — Remove the `in_progress` stage (data not migrated)
- WL-0MTTSWCJR003OMN7 — risk-effort evaluation path (classify maps `in_progress` → `risk-effort`)
- WL-0MTTS9FY00055QJV — RCA: near-zero downtime dispatches (worker-liveness gaps)
- WL-0MTTSWD1E000ZEXR — per-tick dispatcher diagnostics

# Intake Brief: Downtime Worker Over-Dispatch on Single-Slot LLM

## Headline

With a single-slot local LLM, the downtime worker over-dispatches agent panes because it only bounds in-flight dispatch pipelines (not running panes) and ignores the Local Proxy owner lease, causing multiple panes to queue on one slot and starve each other.

## Problem Statement

The downtime worker's free-slot gate and concurrency cap are blind to agent pane ownership and lease state. On a single-slot LLM, this causes multiple concurrent `Downtime triggered` panes to be dispatched, all routing requests through the same proxy slot and creating long contention queues.

## Users

- **Internal operators** running a single-slot local LLM: want downtime panes to be dispatched only when a slot is truly available and not already owned by a running agent pane.
- **herdr infrastructure team**: want the dispatcher to respect the Local Proxy lease protocol to prevent pane contention.

## Existing State

- `downtimeMaxConcurrentDispatches` (default 1) bounds in-flight dispatch *pipelines* only — incremented before claim→marker→spawn and decremented in `finally` (~1–2 s after pane spawns). It does not count running panes.
- Free-slot gate (`freeSlots >= DOWNTIME_PANE_MIN_FREE_SLOTS` = 1) uses instantaneous per-tick proxy poll state. An agent on a tool call (wl, bash, tests) leaves the slot "free".
- Idle threshold is 60 s continuous-idle (10 s polls), re-opening the gate between agent generations.
- Local Proxy `local_owner_session_id` / `local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds` are parsed into `LlamaStatus` but never consulted by the dispatch decision.
- Every dispatched pane acquires a Local Proxy lease via `run-pi-agent.sh` / `release-lease-on-exit.mjs`.

## Symptom / Impact

- Multiple concurrent `Downtime triggered` panes dispatched against 1 slot (e.g., 4 panes in ~5 min on 2026-09-12).
- Proxy reports `contention_queued_count: 6` with ~78 s cumulative queue time — panes queue behind each other.
- Dispatch cadence: ~75–90 s apart after idle threshold is re-met.
- Agents oversubscribed to one slot starve each other.

## Proposed Fix

1. **Rename setting and change semantics** — Rename `downtimeMaxConcurrentDispatches` to `downtimeMaxRunningPanes` (or equivalent). The setting now tracks running panes (alive dispatched agents), not in-flight dispatch pipelines.
2. **Bound running panes, not just pipelines** — Track dispatched panes that are still alive (via `herdr pane list` / dispatch markers with no completion) and refuse new dispatch when running-panes ≥ `downtimeMaxRunningPanes`.
3. **Honour the Local Proxy owner lease** — Treat a non-null `local_owner_session_id` (or lease held by a live dispatch pane) as "slot busy" for the idle/dispatch gate. Only dispatch into a slot that is truly unowned.
4. **Per-slot owner tracking** — Use per-slot owner/lease per `slot_id` in the idle tracker instead of global `available_slots` so an owned slot is never considered available for a new pane.
5. **Contention feedback** — When the proxy reports `contention_queued_count > 0` / queued requests from dispatched panes, back off dispatch until the queue drains.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. With `total_slots = 1`, the worker never keeps more than 1 dispatched downtime pane active per free slot (running-pane bound honoured across roots and across leader/instance restarts).
2. A pane that holds a Local Proxy lease (or whose session id is the proxy's `local_owner_session_id`) prevents a new dispatch into that slot.
3. Regression test: simulate a slot that is idle-but-owned (lease held by a live pane) → no dispatch; and a 1-slot status with an old dispatch pane still running → no new dispatch until the pane exits.
4. The setting has been renamed (`downtimeMaxConcurrentDispatches` → `downtimeMaxRunningPanes` or equivalent) and documented with the new semantics; existing tests and documentation updated.
5. Per-slot owner tracking is implemented so that a slot with a live lease is never considered available for new dispatch.
6. Contention feedback is implemented: when the proxy reports `contention_queued_count > 0`, dispatch backs off until the queue drains.
7. `npm run build` clean and the full suite green.

## Constraints

- Must work correctly across leader/instance restarts (no state loss).
- Must not break multi-slot LLM setups — the fix should be slot-aware.
- Audits already have `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2` (never fire on 1-slot) — no change needed for audit tier.
- The existing lease protocol (`run-pi-agent.sh` / `release-lease-on-exit.mjs`) should be respected, not bypassed.
- Existing tests and documentation must be updated to reflect the renamed setting and new semantics.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Core dispatch logic, idle gate, concurrency cap
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — Existing tests to update
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — `downtimeMaxConcurrentDispatches` configuration
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — Settings registration
- `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh` — Local Proxy lease acquisition
- `packages/herdr/shared/release-lease-on-exit.mjs` — Lease release on pane exit
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — Timing defaults and configuration docs

## Related Work

- **WL-0MT50LKAK001EF5Q** — Allow bounded concurrent downtime dispatches (F2/F3; the cap was implemented as pipeline-only)
- **WL-0MTSAB0QU003KTLA** — `downtimeMaxConcurrentDispatches` setting
- **WL-0MSGI7UIH008USVB** — Herdr plugin: release the Local Proxy model lease when a pi session is closed
- **WL-0MTTSWCJR003OMN7** — Dispatch risk/effort evaluation for plan_complete items
- **WL-0MTYL7DX9000MZOH** — Downtime dispatcher hard-strikes on retired 'in_progress' stage (open, related dispatcher health bug)
- **WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2** — Spare-capacity dispatch (completed)
- **WL-0MTOTCETU004YYIU** — RCA: 3 consecutive CLI errors pausing dispatch (open)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk**: Tracking running panes accurately across restarts may require persisted state. **Mitigation**: Start with in-memory tracking + persistence check on restart (count panes from `herdr pane list` at startup).
- **Risk**: Owner lease check may block dispatch during short idle gaps (tool calls). **Mitigation**: If a pane exits before the next dispatch tick, the slot becomes unowned and available.
- **Risk**: Contentious panes on 1 slot may still queue behind each other. **Mitigation**: Focus on dispatch-level fixes first; contention feedback (fix #4) can be a follow-up.
- **Assumption**: `herdr pane list` reliably reports pane lifecycle state (working/idle/exited).
- **Assumption**: Local Proxy lease protocol (`run-pi-agent.sh` / `release-lease-on-exit.mjs`) is reliable for owner tracking.
- **Scope**: All five fix directions (running-panes bound, owner lease, per-slot tracking, contention feedback) are in scope for this work item.
- **Risk**: Renaming the setting may affect existing user configs. **Mitigation**: Support both old and new names with a deprecation warning during a transition period.

## Problem statement

The Herdr downtime dispatcher never dispatches, even when the local LLM is idle and free, because its contention back-off gate reads the proxy's **cumulative** `contention_queued_count` metric instead of the **live** `contention_queue_depth`. Once any request has ever queued on the proxy process, the cumulative counter stays `> 0` forever, so the worker refuses every dispatch until the proxy process restarts.

### User story

- As an operator, when the local LLM is idle I want the downtime dispatcher to keep dispatching work, so that cheap-mode capacity is not wasted indefinitely.
- As a maintainer, I want the contention gate to use the current queue depth, so that a past contention event does not permanently disable dispatch.

## Evidence (observed 2026-09-14)

Live `GET http://192.168.0.199:8000/llama/local/status`:

```json
{ "llama_server_running": true, "local_active_query": false,
  "model_switch_in_progress": false, "available_slots": 1, "total_slots": 1,
  "slots": [{"slot_id":0,"is_processing":false}],
  "contention_queue_depth": 0,
  "contention_queued_count": 13,
  "contention_queued_duration_seconds": 28.466 }
```

Running the worker's own `parseLlamaStatus` + `isIdleStatus(status, 1)` against that payload:

```text
parse ok: true
isIdleStatus(requiredFreeSlots=1): true          # LLM is idle
worker reads contention_queued_count => 13
=> contention gate blocks dispatch: true
```

Proxy source `projects/llm-manager/proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py`:

```python
def metrics() -> dict:
    """Cumulative queue metrics for the status_request / dispatch logs."""
    return {
        "contention_queue_depth": len(_waiters),   # current depth
        "contention_queued_count": queued_count,   # cumulative (only incremented, L174)
        ...
    }
```

`queued_count` is only ever incremented (`wait_for_local_slot`, L174) and has no production reset (the only reset is the test helper `reset()`), so the dispatcher backs off permanently after the first queue event following a proxy restart.

The last dispatch record is `2026-09-14T05:06:08Z`; the worker kept ticking (leader lease refreshed, coordination check-ins every ~2.5 min, 4 offers in `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json`) but dispatched nothing after that. The contention gate returns a neutral outcome (`dispatched:false, idle:true`) with no log line, so the failure is silent. It only bites in `cheap` mode; the proxy emits the queue fields only then.

Introduced by `fc5f9c4f` (WL-0MTYZXSLN008HZOW, AC6), including the wrong field name in tests, fixtures and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.

## Desired change

Use the proxy's current queue depth (`contention_queue_depth`) as the contention back-off signal. The cumulative `contention_queued_count` may be retained for telemetry but must not gate dispatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Current-depth gate** — `parseLlamaStatus` parses `contention_queue_depth` (non-negative finite number; malformed/negative → `null`/busy, fail-closed) and the dispatcher blocks dispatch only while the parsed current depth is `> 0`. A test proves that a payload with `contention_queue_depth: 0` and `contention_queued_count: 13` does **not** block dispatch.
2. **Cumulative counter decoupled** — `contention_queued_count` (cumulative) is never used for the dispatch/back-off decision. A test asserts the two fields are distinct and that a large cumulative count with depth 0 dispatches.
3. **Back-compat** — a pre-feature payload without `contention_queue_depth` leaves the gate disabled (treated as 0, no contention evidence), matching the existing optional-field contract; malformed values remain fail-closed.
4. **Docs corrected** — `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (contention feedback section) and the field doc comments/tests/fixtures refer to `contention_queue_depth` as the gate signal and describe `contention_queued_count` as cumulative telemetry.
5. **Regression coverage** — a test reproduces the wedge: a cumulative count `> 0` with depth `0` dispatches; a depth `> 0` backs off with reason `proxy-contention`.

## In scope

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `LlamaStatus`, `parseLlamaStatus`, the tick contention gate, `dispatchDowntimeWork` contention gate.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fixtures.ts`.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.

## Out of scope

- Changing the proxy (`llm-manager`) metrics.
- Any change to idle detection, running-pane bound, or owner-lease gates.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: `contention_queue_depth` is the intended "requests currently queued behind a busy local slot" signal (matches the existing doc wording).
- Risk: proxies that serve only the legacy cumulative field would disable the gate; acceptable because the depth field ships with the same proxy feature and absence already means "no contention evidence".

# Remove the client-side running-pane cap from the downtime dispatcher (LLM idle check must be the only limiter)

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher stopped dispatching after a single item. It should keep
dispatching throughout idle periods for as long as the local LLM is idle; the
LLM idle check is the natural concurrency limiter (each running agent holds a
proxy slot/lease). Instead, a **client-side cap on the number of live panes**
exists and, because dispatched panes deliberately stay open until an operator
closes them, the cap never releases.

Observed 2026-09-14/15: exactly one item dispatched overnight (and nothing
across several roots for many hours); the next item dispatched *immediately*
after the operator closed the open dispatcher pane. Live evidence at
investigation time: exactly one `Downtime` pane (`w0:p2`, `agent_status`
`working`) was present, saturating the cap.

Regression source: `WL-0MTYZXSLN008HZOW` (commit `fc5f9c4f`, 2026-09-13) fixed
genuine over-dispatch on a single-slot LLM, but as part of that renamed
`downtimeMaxConcurrentDispatches` → `downtimeMaxRunningPanes` **in place, keeping
the default value `1`, while changing its meaning**:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Setting | `downtimeMaxConcurrentDispatches = 1` | `downtimeMaxRunningPanes = 1` |
| Counted | in-flight dispatch **pipelines** (~1-2 s, released in `finally` after spawn) | live **panes** |
| Releases | automatically, milliseconds later | only when an operator closes the pane |

With panes intentionally persistent, "max 1 live pane" means exactly one
dispatch per operator pane-close. The refusal is neutral and silent — no
strike, no cooldown, no log line — so it presented as "nothing is happening".

## Users

- **Operator / producer** — expects overnight downtime dispatch to keep working
  through the backlog whenever the local LLM is idle; sees stalls instead.
  - "As an operator, when the local LLM is idle I want the next work item
    dispatched, regardless of how many previously dispatched panes are still
    open, so overnight capacity is used."
  - "As an operator, I want dispatched panes to stay open until I close them, so
    I can inspect what each agent did."
- **Dispatch operator (herdr)** — needs the dispatcher to make progress on the
  backlog across roots without manual pane intervention.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **No pane-count refusal**: with an idle LLM (idle threshold met and free
   slots >= the tier minimum) and one *or more* live `Downtime` panes present,
   the worker still dispatches. Regression test reproducing the overnight stall
   (live panes present + idle LLM -> dispatch happens).
2. **`running-pane-cap` is gone**: no dispatch path refuses based on the number
   of live panes; the `running-pane-cap` outcome reason no longer exists in the
   codebase.
3. **Idle gate unchanged**: while the proxy reports non-idle (busy slot, active
   query, active lease, or insufficient free slots) dispatch is still refused —
   the LLM idle check remains the concurrency limiter.
4. **Non-count protections preserved**: the owner-lease gate (`slotOwned`) and
   the proxy-contention gate (`contentionQueueDepth`) still refuse dispatch, so
   removing the pane count does not reintroduce over-dispatch into an owned slot.
5. **Pipeline single-flight retained**: the same-process in-flight *pipeline*
   guard still refuses a second overlapping pipeline with reason
   `dispatch-in-flight`, at a fixed single-flight bound of 1 (not derived from
   any setting).
6. **Setting removed**: `downtimeMaxRunningPanes` is removed from
   `PluginSettings` and the defaults; the legacy `downtimeMaxConcurrentDispatches`
   key is removed as well. A settings file carrying either key loads cleanly with
   no error and neither key influences dispatch. `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MAX_RUNNING_PANES`,
   `clampDowntimeMaxRunningPanes` and their deprecated aliases are removed.
7. **Failed liveness query does not stall dispatch**: a failing
   `getRunningDowntimePanes` query no longer blocks dispatch; it only affects the
   `slotOwned` qualifier, and the proxy's own lease/ownership signals still gate.
8. **Panes are never auto-closed**: this change introduces no pane-close or
   pane-kill behaviour; dispatched panes continue to stay open until an operator
   closes them.
9. **Docs and tests**: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` is updated (the
   running-pane-bound section is replaced by the "LLM idle check is the sole
   limiter; panes persist until closed" contract, and the settings-table row is
   removed); `packages/herdr/README.md` is updated if it mentions the setting.
   Unit tests are added/updated for AC1-AC7.
10. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Do not** make dispatched panes self-terminate. Panes stay open until an
  operator closes them; that is intended behaviour (WL-0MS9HIUE0002JAKQ family:
  panes left open for inspection).
- Keep the LLM idle/free-slot gate as the single capacity authority; do not add
  any other client-side concurrency limit in its place.
- Keep the proxy-side protections added by `WL-0MTYZXSLN008HZOW` that are *not*
  a client-side count: the owner-lease gate and contention back-off. Only the
  pane count is being removed.
- Surgical change: no unrelated refactoring of the dispatcher.
- Backward compatibility for settings files: unknown/removed keys must not cause
  a load error.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:212` — `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MAX_RUNNING_PANES = 1`
  (+ deprecated `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MAX_CONCURRENT_DISPATCHES` alias).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:5182-5190` — `clampDowntimeMaxRunningPanes`
  (+ deprecated alias).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:4025-4026` — the tick derives
  `maxRunningPanes` from `cfg.maxRunningPanes ?? cfg.maxConcurrentDispatches ?? default`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:4062-4064` — **the live blocker**:
  `runningPanes >= maxRunningPanes` -> `return { dispatched: false, idle: true }`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:4103-4112` — the tick passes
  `maxRunningPanes` into the legacy `dispatchDowntimeWork` fallback.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:2790-2793` — legacy path refuses with
  `reason: 'running-pane-cap'`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:1219-1230` — `countRunningDowntimePanes`
  counts panes whose label starts with `Downtime` and which host a live pi agent
  (status not `done`/`exited`); an agent that has finished but whose pane is
  still open is still counted (the reason the cap never releases).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:4046` — `slotOwned = ownerLeaseHeld && (runningPanes ?? 0) > 0`
  (retained).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts:1362` — `maxRunningPanes: s.downtimeMaxRunningPanes` wiring.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts:101,125,238-243` — field, default, and old-key migration.
- Proxy lease semantics (verified, `projects/llm-manager/proxy`): leases carry an
  `expires_at` (`router_helpers.py:612-617`, default 180 s), are marked inactive
  when a stream ends (`router_helpers.py:941`) and expired records are cleaned up
  (`router_helpers.py:1440-1476`). The lease signal therefore **self-heals**; the
  pane count does not.

## Desired change

Restore the intended dispatch contract:

1. Check the local LLM is idle (idle threshold + free slots, lease-aware) — if
   not, stop. *(unchanged)*
2. Select the next work item. *(unchanged)*
3. Ensure the Dispatcher workspace/anchor exists, creating it if not. *(unchanged)*
4. Spawn a pane in that workspace running an agent on the work item. *(unchanged)*

Remove only the client-side pane-count bound: both refusal sites, the setting and
its clamp/default plumbing, and the now-unnecessary fail-closed liveness gate.
Retain the pipeline single-flight guard, the owner-lease gate and the contention
gate.

## Key files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — remove the pane-count refusals (tick
  ~4062, legacy ~2790), remove `maxRunningPanes`/`maxConcurrentDispatches` plumbing
  and the clamp/default constants, keep `dispatchInFlightCount` single-flight at 1,
  keep `slotOwned` / `contentionQueueDepth`, and update `countRunningDowntimePanes`
  doc comment (now only feeds `slotOwned`).
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — drop `downtimeMaxRunningPanes` (field,
  default, legacy-key migration) and the imports.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — drop the `maxRunningPanes` config wiring.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — remove `running-pane-cap`
  assertions; add the AC1/AC5/AC7 regression tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.test.ts` — remove the `downtimeMaxRunningPanes` and
  `clampDowntimeMaxRunningPanes` / default-constant tests; add an AC6 test that a
  config carrying the removed keys still loads.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — replace the running-pane-bound section and
  the settings-table row.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — update if the setting is documented.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (medium): reintroducing over-dispatch.** `WL-0MTYZXSLN008HZOW` was raised
  because 4-7 panes queued on one slot. Mitigation: the proxy-side protections
  added by that item are retained — the owner-lease signal already inside the idle
  gate (`local_lease_active`) and `countFreeUnownedSlots`, the `slotOwned` gate,
  and `contentionQueueDepth` back-off. Those are lease/ownership based and
  self-heal on lease expiry, unlike the pane count. Verified lease TTL/expiry
  behaviour in the proxy source.
- **Risk (low): a failed `herdr pane list` query previously stalled all dispatch
  (fail-closed).** After this change it no longer blocks. Accepted: the query only
  feeds the `slotOwned` qualifier, and the proxy lease/ownership signals remain
  authoritative.
- **Known caveat (documented, not fixed here):** `slotOwned = ownerLeaseHeld &&
  (runningPanes ?? 0) > 0` was qualified by "the worker has no running pane of its
  own" so an operator's own lease would not block spare-capacity dispatch. Since
  dispatched panes now persist indefinitely, that qualifier is effectively always
  true while any `Downtime` pane is open, degenerating `slotOwned` to
  `ownerLeaseHeld`. Leases expire (~180 s), so this self-heals and does not stall
  an unattended run; on a single-slot setup it is also redundant with the
  `local_lease_active` check already inside the idle gate. Not changed here to keep
  the change surgical — if it proves to suppress spare-capacity dispatch during an
  operator's own session, raise it as a separate item.
- **Assumption:** the LLM idle check (plus proxy lease signals) is a sufficient
  concurrency limiter, per the operator's stated design.
- **Supersedes:** AC1/AC3 of `WL-0MTYZXSLN008HZOW` (the running-pane bound) are
  reversed by this item; the rest of that item is preserved.

## Related work

- `WL-0MTYZXSLN008HZOW` (completed) — introduced the running-pane bound being
  removed here; its owner-lease / per-slot-ownership / contention fixes are kept.
- `WL-0MTYZXSLN008HZOW` child `WL-0MT3PHW4I002SNOV` — audit single-flight (a
  separate, intentional single-flight; unaffected).
- `WL-0MS9HIUE0002JAKQ` (completed) — panes stay open for inspection; the
  behaviour this item must preserve.
- `WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG` / `WL-0MTR2CD4X006XI7U` — the dedicated Dispatcher
  workspace anchor used for step 3 of the contract.
- `WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2` — spare-capacity dispatch (per-slot free-slot minimums);
  context for the `slotOwned` caveat above.
- Discovered from: `WL-0MTYZXSLN008HZOW`.

# Child 1: Re-sort no longer invalidates previously fresh audits via `updatedAt` churn

Parent: WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 (mechanism 1).

## Problem statement

`batchUpdateSortIndices` in `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769` stamps `updatedAt = now` alongside `sortIndex` in a single SQL UPDATE:

```sql
UPDATE workitems SET sortIndex = ?, updatedAt = ? WHERE id = ?
```

This means any re-sort operation (triggered automatically on `wl next` unless `--no-re-sort`) bumps the `updatedAt` of every item whose sortIndex changed. The audit-freshness rule (`isAuditNotReadyFresh`, `database.ts:644`) checks `auditedAt >= updatedAt` — so a re-sort after an audit silently invalidates a previously passing audit.

**Evidence:** 13 items share identical `updatedAt=2026-09-11T07:34:26.956Z` with consecutive sortIndex 300-1500; another 88-item cluster at `2026-09-11T08:33:19.554Z`. WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V's passing audit is stale after re-sort.

## Root cause

Sort index is an organizational/concern, not a semantic change. The `updatedAt` field is used by the audit freshness invariant as a proxy for "when did this item last change semantically". Stamping `updatedAt` during sortIndex-only updates conflates mechanical churn with semantic edits.

## Solution

Remove `updatedAt = ?` from the sortIndex-only UPDATE in `batchUpdateSortIndices`. This is a surgical change to a single SQL statement.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `batchUpdateSortIndices` does NOT update `updatedAt` — sortIndex changes are transparent to audit freshness
- [ ] An item with a passing audit (`readyToClose: true`) retains audit freshness across re-sort operations (auditedAt >= updatedAt still holds)
- [ ] Genuine semantic edits (description, title, status, etc.) still bump `updatedAt` — the freshness invariant works correctly for real changes
- [ ] Existing tests for updatedAt preservation (whitespace-only diffs, CAS claims, etc.) still pass
- [ ] New regression test: audit item → re-sort → verify audit still fresh
- [ ] Full project test suite passes

## Constraints

- Minimal change: only modify the SQL in `batchUpdateSortIndices`
- Do not break the existing updatedAt preservation behavior for genuine edits (the update/import/upsert no-op guards already handle this)
- No schema migration needed
- The `reSort` function in database.ts calls `assignSortIndexValuesForItems` → `batchUpdateSortIndices`; only the SQL statement changes

## Key files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — `batchUpdateSortIndices` (line ~747-769)
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `reSort`, `isAuditNotReadyFresh`, `assignSortIndexValuesForItems`
- `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts` — existing updatedAt tests

## Parent AC coverage

- **Parent WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 AC1:** Re-sort no longer invalidates previously fresh audits — this is the primary fix.
- **Parent WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 AC3:** Queue surfaces distinguish semantic edits from mechanical timestamp churn — fixing updatedAt churn at the source enables this.
- **Parent WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 AC4:** New regression test: audit → re-sort → verify freshness.
- **Parent WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 AC5:** Full suite passes (all children contribute).

## Related work

- Parent: WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9
